sn38.3:1.2: “Those who teach principles” or “those who teach Dhamma” (_dhammavādino_).
sn38.3:1.4: “Holy One” (_sugata_) is a frequent epithet of the Buddha, or as here, for any arahant. Formally, it parallels “Realized One” (_tathāgata_), i.e. “one who has come to the state of truth”. _Sugata_ therefore means “one who has come to the state of the good/happy/well”. These are past participles; the noun form of the same word is _sugati_, a “good place” or “heaven”. It is primarily associated with Buddhism (Agni Purāṇa 360.3); in later Sanskrit, followers of the Buddha were called _bauddha_ or _saugata_.
